text:
PA UFOs! An interview with MUFON's Jim Krug
The UFO Tourist discusses Blue Beam, Bigfoot, and Bar Tabs.
MUFON investigator Jim Krug has credentials. He graduated from Juniata College in 2002 with a Bachelor’s in Science and in Earth & Space Science and Secondary Education. He’s served as the Director of the Neil Armstrong Planetarium in Altoona, PA since 2003, co-founded the Space Race Museum containing valuable artifacts from the US and Soviet Space programs, and founded the Mt. Lion Observatory at the nearby Fort Roberdeau historic site.
Krug has been a MUFON Field Investigator since 2015, and a PA State Section Director since 2017. He is a member of MUFON’s Experiencer Resource Team (ERT), which investigates Close Encounters of the 4th Kind and beyond. Jim is a frequent presenter at UFO Conferences and has made many media appearances in addition to co-hosting the Majestic Ears Only podcast. His unique background and experience give him insight on the intersection between astronomy and UFOs.
B: Thank you for your time today, Jim.
JK: My pleasure.
B: How did you become interested in UFOs?
JK: When I was very young, mid-1980s, I was at a neighbor’s house to watch a movie. Prior to the movie, he was playing a PBS show hosted by a couple of scientists featuring pictures of classic UFOs and flying saucers. Naturally, I expected them to be making fun of the photos, but they were taking the subject seriously. That made me think: maybe there’s something to this whole UFO thing, after all?
B: Have you had any first hand UFO experiences?
JK: I’ve had two UFO sightings in my life. One happened at an amusement park at night when a friend and I saw a triangular UFO move over the park before suddenly turning in the opposite direction. It was directly overhead, but we were the only ones paying attention and looking up! My second sighting was on a highway 15 miles from home, in an area I know well. I saw what looked like a very low, white meteor shoot across the sky and disappear—but at the end of its path was a wide, ruddy red object hovering over the small town of Claysburg, PA. I regret not pulling over to watch it further as it lingered a few hundred feet over the town.
B: How does being an astronomer help you investigate UFOs?
JK: I’ve taught astronomy at the high school level for 23 years and am the planetarium director of the
[Neil Armstrong Planetarium]—roles that have allowed me to see how astronomy intersects with the possibility of extraterrestrial life. In my 10 years as a UFO investigator for MUFON, I’ve found that it’s easy for people to misidentify Venus or other celestial bodies. Most cases are submitted from well-meaning people who have never taken a good look at the nighttime sky. My background helps me find natural explanations when they are available.
B: What do your students think about UFOs?
JK: Surprisingly, my high school students are not as interested as you might think! Unlike older generations, I think these students accept the fact that we’re not alone in the universe, so the idea isn’t as dramatic for them. It’s challenging as a teacher to present the topic in an abbreviated fashion, since so much foundational explanation is needed. I try to give my students a well-rounded take, from astronomers assessing the possibility of alien life, to recent disclosures from Capitol Hill, to some of the best cases of classic UFOlogy.
B: How does Pennsylvania stack up in terms of UFO sightings?
JK: Pennsylvania is usually top five nationwide in UFO sightings. Reports typically correlate with population, so I don’t think it’s a coincidence that the most populous states also have the most sightings.
People incorrectly assume that the larger western states don’t have a lot of UFO activity. I think it’s fairly widespread across the country, but in the population centers, it gets more notice. Pennsylvania specifically is a hotbed of supernatural activity. As one of the original 13 colonies, we have a long history of ghost stories and reported paranormal phenomena. Bigfoot even makes a cameo here and there.
B: Have you investigated many Bigfoot cases?
JK: Absolutely. This particularly fascinating aspect of the phenomenon is detailed in the work of investigator and author, Stan Gordon. He’s conducted remarkable research on the topic in his book, Silent Invasion, the Pennsylvania Bigfoot UFO Casebook. In the early 1970s, there was a huge flap here in PA. (“Flap” is the term we use in UFOlogy to recognize a sudden increase in UFO sightings in a particular geographic area.) This flap occurred across the southwestern United States, Pittsburgh, and as far east as Altoona. Along with UFO sightings, there were also increased reports of Bigfoot activity.
B: There seems to be an association between the Big Guy and orbs—have you come across any such cases?
JK: I have not had a Bigfoot orb case myself, but I do think there’s a grand unifying theory between the various paranormal phenomena. We should embrace all of these aspects—from cryptids to UFOs—because once you delve into it, you see there’s a lot of interconnectedness.
B: That harkens back to John Keel and Jacques Vallée and their conclusions about paranormal and folkloric connections. Their research efforts lead them to independently consider a possible paranormal vs. extraterrestrial explanation for UFOs. Their theories were considered fringe at the time (1969–1970), but today their line of thinking is embraced.
JK: They were trailblazers, yes. I think their work changed UFOlogy for the better.
B: I completely agree with you. The “Nuts and Bolts” theory has met its match.
JK: UFOlogy has evolved from only being interested in strange lights in the sky—a paranormal Pandora’s box has been opened, and we haven’t been able to shut it since.
B: Let’s Revisit MUFON for a moment. Why do you think MUFON survived when all the other civilian organizations didn’t?
JK: Other civilian organizations were infiltrated by U.S. intelligence agencies. Take NICAP, the National Investigative Committee of Aerial Phenomenon, founded in 1956. Its aim was to push for Congressional investigations into UFOs. They had many well-respected scientists, ex-government officials, ex-military, and media people as paying members. In subsequent decades we’ve learned that intelligence agencies not only infiltrated them, but placed some of their own people into leadership positions. They paid themselves large salaries, leased lavish offices in Washington, D.C., and eventually bankrupted the organization.
To MUFON’s credit, it has remained grassroots, small budget, and mostly filled with ranks of people who have a genuine interest in the phenomenon, combined with a desire to help experiencers. MUFON’s structure and nature have given it longevity.
B: MUFON has grown exponentially since Walter Andrus started it in 1969, and to this day, they still maintain high standards for field research.
JK: It’s a constant arms race between MUFON and the other organizations out there. The biggest challenge to MUFON is smaller startup groups that seem to be very well-funded. Their generous budgets allow them to invest in SEO (Search Engine Optimization) so that when people search the internet for where to report a UFO sighting, these smaller organizations appear as the top search results. The last time I checked, MUFON was way down at the bottom of Google’s first page. If MUFON doesn’t receive these raw reports, it’s akin to expecting a tree to grow by cutting off all the roots.
B: Can you share a memorable Pennsylvania case—one that keeps you up at night?
JK: I’m sure a lot of your readers are familiar with Pennsylvania UFO lore and know about the legendary
[Kecksburg UFO]crash just outside of Pittsburgh, where it’s claimed that the military recovered an acorn-shaped, crashed ship. Sometimes it takes a person years, even decades, to report a UFO. This was the case in 2020, when a witness contacted me about a sighting they had in December, 1963—the same timeframe as the Kecksburg UFO crash. They were driving home from school during daylight hours and came upon a mess of cars pulled off to the side of the road. The witness stopped to see what the commotion was about and saw “an acorn shaped ship floating in a clearing over a power line.” He added that “it wasn’t working properly.” My immediate reply was “Well, how’s an acorn-shaped ship supposed to work?”
B: What was the witness’ response?
JK: He said he knew something was wrong because, “the ship was listing to one side and shooting sparks out of it.” It eventually shot off to the west and disappeared. His report suggests that it might not be extraterrestrials. The craft’s “malfunctions” could be evidence that the United States government was working with some type of early anti-gravity technology, possibly brought over with the Germans in Operation Paperclip at the end of World War Two. Maybe it’s the same craft that crashed near Kecksburg a few days later. It would explain how the military appeared so quickly on the scene to retrieve it.
B: Interesting, because in your talk at the First Annual Jim Thorpe ParaCon, you mentioned secret German technology. There’s a lot of speculation regarding technologies like the German Bell and other Nazi saucers.
JK: Oh, yes. The Bell: Die Glocken, and the Haunebu Flying Saucer.
B: I think the most important question for readers of THE OBSERVER is this: As a UFO investigator, how do you view the current state of UFOlogy?
JK: I think all of the revelations coming out are very exciting, but I would urge your readers to exercise caution when looking at these claims. Take it from someone who has dealt with government secrets for decades. It’s somewhat unsettling that all this new “information” is being given so freely to us. The question should be: “Why all of a sudden?”
B: Do you think there could be more going on than just hiding the truth about extraterrestrials?
JK: I would encourage your readers to research an idea called
[Project Blue Beam]. Some people suggest that this technology will be used to fake an alien invasion in hopes of bringing about a one world government.
After decades of official secrecy, we should heed the old saying about the Trojan Horse: “Beware of Greeks bearing gifts.” With whistleblowers coming forward and UFOs and aliens constantly in the headlines, are we being prepared for Disclosure? Or could this be the prelude to a larger deception? Who is really “bearing” these gifts?
B: Sort of what John Keel described in Operation Trojan Horse, or like Jacques Vallée’s “control system” in Messengers of Deception.
JK: Yes, exactly.
B: Jim, I really appreciate you sharing your encyclopedic knowledge of UFOs with our readers. Your firsthand investigative experiences makes your comments even more valuable to the UFOlogicial community.
JK: Thank you, Bernie. I hope to see your readers at one of our upcoming conventions!
(At the end of the interview, the theater manager asked which one of us was picking up the tab, and Jim pointed at me. I hope the editor approves the expense—it was worth it!)
To report a UFO, Bigfoot or any other paranormal activity in PA, please visit the MUFON website. Jim Krug can be found in Section 6.
